chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Amr from 'Amr ibn Sa'idr from al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm and Ibn Faddal said: We asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him)
about al-fuqqah (a fermented drink) so he said: 'It is an unknown wine, and in it is the penalty of the drinker of wine.'

key_terms.الْفُقَّاعُ: A specific fermented drink, often made from grains or fruits, discussed in classical fiqh.
key_terms.حَدُّ: The fixed legal penalty prescribed in Islamic law for a specific crime.
key_terms.خَمْرٌ مَجْهُولٌ: Unknown wine; a legal category where a drink is treated as wine due to its intoxicating nature despite unclear origin.
key_terms.شَارِبِ الْخَمْرِ: The drinker of wine, the subject of the penalty.

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling on the fermented drink known as Fuqqah in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) ruled that al-fuqqah, a specific fermented beverage, is considered a type of wine (khamr) even if its specific identity or origin is not widely known, and therefore carries the hadd (fixed legal penalty) of wine drinkers. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of 'istishab al-hukm' (presumption of continuity), where a substance retains the ruling of wine once it undergoes fermentation, regardless of its specific name or source. It underscores the importance of the physical process of fermentation over nomenclature in determining intoxicants.
